title: HRIPCB: a challenging dataset for PCB defects detection and classification
authors: Weibo Huang; Peng Wei; Manhua Zhang; Hong Liu
organization: Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School; Shenzhen Skyworth-RGB Electronic Co., Ltd.
venue: The Journal of Engineering, vol. 2020, iss. 13, pp. 303-309
used_for: Dataset identity, acquisition setup, class definitions, and the 1386-image description
verified_claim: Journal names the dataset HRIPCB and states 1386 synthesized images, six defect types, 10 template boards, a 16-megapixel CMOS camera, 4608x3456 capture, and Photoshop-made defects. Table 1 lists the non-rotated half because the rotated half has the same counts.

title: A PCB Dataset for Defects Detection and Classification
used_for: Earlier public version cited by the course proposal
verified_claim: Submitted 24 January 2019. Lists two authors and the same 1386-image description. The proposal citation [7] matches this preprint, not the later four-author journal version.

title: PCB-DATASET repository
used_for: Dataset distribution used in this project
verified_claim: README points to the IET paper and the arXiv preprint. The checkout used here contains an images folder, an Annotations folder, a rotation folder, and PCB_USED.

title: Online PCB Defect Detector On A New PCB Defect Dataset
authors: Sanli Tang; Fan He; Xiaolin Huang; Jie Yang
used_for: DeepPCB is a different dataset from HRIPCB
verified_claim: DeepPCB has 1,500 image pairs, 1,000 for training and 500 for testing. Classes are open, short, mousebite, spur, pin-hole, and spurious copper. Reported result is 98.6 percent mAP at 62 FPS. A detection is counted when IoU exceeds 0.33.

title: DeepPCB repository
used_for: DeepPCB distribution and research-use notice
verified_claim: README describes 1,500 pairs of 640x640 images and states that the dataset may be used for research.

title: An Improved YOLOv5 Network for Detection of Printed Circuit Board Defects
authors: Jie Niu; Hongyan Li; Xu Chen; Kun Qian
used_for: Published YOLOv5 PCB detector used as related work
verified_claim: The paper reports 99.1 percent mean average precision at 86 frames per second on a public defect dataset. This audit does not treat that number as a result of the present experiment.

title: PCB defect detection algorithm based on CDI-YOLO
authors: Gaoshang Xiao; Shuling Hou; Huiying Zhou
used_for: Related PCB detector and a second description of the Peking University images
verified_claim: CDI-YOLO, based on YOLOv7-tiny, reports 98.3 percent mAP. The authors say they started from 693 Peking University images and cropped them to 10,668 images. That mAP is not a result on the uncropped test split used here.

title: Physical Adversarial Examples for Object Detectors
authors: Kevin Eykholt; Ivan Evtimov; Earlence Fernandes; Bo Li; Amir Rahmati; Florian Tramer; Atul Prakash; Tadayoshi Kohno; Dawn Song
used_for: Literature on physical disappearance attacks against detectors
verified_claim: Reports a disappearance attack against YOLOv2. In the indoor poster and sticker tests, a Stop sign was missed in 85.6 percent and 85.0 percent of frames. This project does not repeat that physical attack.

title: On Physical Adversarial Patches for Object Detection
used_for: Literature on localized patches that suppress YOLOv3 detections
verified_claim: Describes a patch that can suppress YOLOv3 detections, including objects that are not covered by the patch. This project uses a gray occlusion over annotated boxes and does not optimize a patch.

title: Adversarial Patch
authors: Tom B. Brown; Dandelion Mane; Aurko Roy; Martin Abadi; Justin Gilmer
used_for: Literature on universal adversarial patches for classifiers
verified_claim: Introduces a printable targeted patch for image classifiers. Cited as background, not as a method implemented here.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
used_for: Governance structure: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage
verified_claim: NIST AI 100-1, January 2023. The Core has four functions. Govern is cross-cutting. The functions are not a checklist.

title: NIST AI RMF Playbook
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
used_for: Suggested actions for the four AI RMF functions
verified_claim: NIST states that the Playbook is based on AI RMF 1.0, released 26 January 2023.

title: MITRE ATLAS content version 2026.10
used_for: Technique names, identifiers, descriptions, and mitigations
verified_claim: Collection version 2026.10, modified 2026-10-28. Technique pages are cited as https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.Txxxx, which is the path used inside the ATLAS data.

title: Ultralytics YOLOv5 documentation
used_for: Model family actually loaded
verified_claim: Documents YOLOv5u as the Ultralytics-library form of YOLOv5 and gives yolov5su.pt as the small checkpoint. It states that checkpoints trained in the original yolov5 repository are not compatible with the Ultralytics library.

title: Ultralytics YOLOv5 repository
used_for: Public YOLOv5 implementation and default detect.py thresholds
verified_claim: detect.py defaults, as published in the repository, are yolov5s.pt, image size 640, confidence 0.25, and NMS IoU 0.45.

title: Ultralytics prediction configuration
used_for: Current library inference defaults
verified_claim: The prediction configuration documents conf=0.25 and imgsz=640. This audit sets NMS IoU explicitly to 0.45 so the threshold matches YOLOv5 detect.py rather than a later library default.

title: OpenCV documentation
used_for: Implementation of blur, geometric warps, resize, and JPEG encoding
verified_claim: The installed package version is recorded in results/environment.json from the run, not assumed from the documentation.

title: NumPy documentation
used_for: Noise generation and numeric metric calculations
verified_claim: Used for Gaussian noise and metric aggregation. The installed version is recorded in results/environment.json.

title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
authors: Tsung-Yi Lin; Michael Maire; Serge Belongie; James Hays; Pietro Perona; Deva Ramanan; Piotr Dollar; C. Lawrence Zitnick
used_for: Origin of the detection average-precision protocol adapted in this audit
verified_claim: Cited for the COCO detection-evaluation tradition. The exact 101-point interpolation implemented here is defined in the project code and is not claimed to be a byte-for-byte copy of the COCO API.

title: CMPE 253 project proposal
used_for: Scope, research question, and the dataset wording that required verification
verified_claim: The proposal names both DeepPCB and the Huang and Wei dataset and gives 1386 images with six classes for the latter.
